title: Orientation-dependent plastic deformation mechanisms and competition with stress-induced phase transformation in microscale NiTi

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Why microscale NiTi deforms by stress-induced transformation in some orientations and by plasticity in others is unexplained. Because transformation, slip and deformation twinning have different orientation-dependent Schmid factors, the active mode should switch with the compression axis.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/treatment), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The solutionized alloy is B2 austenite with a trace of Ti4Ni2O. Plastic deformation of the [001] pillar is localized to one narrow band; the rest of the pillar shaft stays featureless.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (STR/phase/identity), n10 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n11 (STR/defect/extended), n14 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n15 (STR/phase/identity), n16 (STR/defect/extended). Premises: (001)B19' compound twins a few nanometres wide have been reported before in NiTi shape memory alloys

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: [001]-oriented pillars are superelastic: a stress-induced transformation plateau from ~430 MPa and hysteresis loops that close on unloading. [112]-oriented pillars are not superelastic: unloading is linear and ~12% of the strain is permanent.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (PRP/value), n13 (PRP/behavior_class), n17 (MEC/identification), n18 (PRP/value), n19 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Conventional theory of martensite: B2-B19' with [011]B19' type II twins as lattice-invariant shear cannot produce (001)B19' compound twins; Schmid law: resolved shear stress equals applied stress times the Schmid factor, so the CRSS of one mechanism must be orientation independent

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Orientation decides whether microscale NiTi deforms by herringbone stress-induced MT with superelastic recovery ([001]) or by {011}<100> slip with permanent strain ([112])

nodes.title: MICRO, F3, F5
nodes.head: [001] pillar after deformation: a few fine surface traces confined to one band near the pillar top, the shaft below staying smooth. The austenite islands of the [112] pillar show line contrast on one (-110) trace direction only, with no twin lamellae inside the austenite
nodes.solves: Plastic deformation of the [001] pillar is localized to one narrow band; the rest of the pillar shaft stays featureless
nodes.note: only two austenite islands are in the field, so the absence of austenite twins is weakly supported
nodes.necessity_reason: n10, n14 keeps shown support from o9, o8, o13 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F3
nodes.head: [112] pillar after deformation: dense parallel slip traces over the whole gauge length with a visible shear offset at the pillar base

nodes.head: HR-TEM: four martensite domains M1-M4 meet along sharp boundaries in a herringbone arrangement, the internal line contrast reversing direction from domain to domain
nodes.solves: The martensite domains are built of (001)B19' compound twins a few nanometres wide, arranged in a herringbone structure

nodes.title: evidence, F2, F3
nodes.head: All three [001] load-unload cycles trace closed hysteresis loops with a ~400-500 MPa forward plateau; the third cycle reaches ~1850 MPa. [001] curve: transformation plateau from ~430 MPa, a strain burst at ~910 MPa carrying the pillar from ~5.7% to ~12% strain, and ~7.3% residual strain at the reload arrow
nodes.solves: [001]-oriented pillars are superelastic: a stress-induced transformation plateau from ~430 MPa and hysteresis loops that close on unloading
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point, read trend
nodes.note: cycles 2 and 3 are drawn shifted by +10% and +20% engineering strain; the per-cycle remnant strains quoted in the linked text (0.18/0.28/0.35%) are far below what the axis resolves the linked text quotes 427 +/- 28 MPa for the plateau and 1177 +/- 321 MPa for the burst as averages over several pillars; this particular curve bursts near 910 MPa
nodes.detail: o3: All three [001] load-unload cycles trace closed hysteresis loops with a ~400-500 MPa forward plateau; the third cycle reaches ~1850 MPa; o5: [001] curve: transformation plateau from ~430 MPa, a strain burst at ~910 MPa carrying the pillar from ~5.7% to ~12% strain, and ~7.3% residual strain at the reload arrow
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n9 keeps shown support from o4, o12.

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: [112] curve: a small burst at ~450 MPa, a large burst at ~595 MPa running to ~13.5% strain, then a straight unloading line leaving ~12% strain
nodes.solves: [112]-oriented pillars are not superelastic: unloading is linear and ~12% of the strain is permanent
nodes.note: the linked text quotes 463 +/- 93 MPa and 620 +/- 36 MPa as averages; the values read here sit inside that scatter
nodes.detail: o7: [112] curve: a small burst at ~450 MPa, a large burst at ~595 MPa running to ~13.5% strain, then a straight unloading line leaving ~12% strain

nodes.title: evidence, F7
nodes.head: Schmid factors at [001] and [-112]: {011}<100> slip 0 and 0.471; {001}<100> slip 0 and 0.333; {114}<22-1> twinning 0.314 and 0.471; {112}<-1-11> twinning 0.471 and 0.314. MT Schmid factors: conventional B2-B19' 0.386 at [001], 0.439 at [-112], maximum 0.513 near [-149], minimum 0.253 at [-111]; herringbone 0.520 at [001], 0.348 at [-112], minimum 0.169 at [011]
nodes.solves: Orientation sets the competition: at [001] slip has zero Schmid factor while herringbone MT (0.520) and {112}<111> twinning (0.471) are near maximal, whereas at [112] {011}<100> slip is near maximal (0.471) and herringbone MT only 0.348
nodes.note: the panels are contour maps over the standard stereographic triangle; F7b is OCR-lettered 'q' but the panel itself reads (b)
nodes.detail: o19: Schmid factors at [001] and [-112]: {011}<100> slip 0 and 0.471; {001}<100> slip 0 and 0.333; {114}<22-1> twinning 0.314 and 0.471; {112}<-1-11> twinning 0.471 and 0.314; o20: MT Schmid factors: conventional B2-B19' 0.386 at [001], 0.439 at [-112], maximum 0.513 near [-149], minimum 0.253 at [-111]; herringbone 0.520 at [001], 0.348 at [-112], minimum 0.169 at [011]
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n19 (o19, o20).

nodes.title: ATOM:MD, F8
nodes.head: MD transformation stress is lowest at the [001] corner (~150-250 MPa) and rises toward [-111] (~1000-1200 MPa), the [112] region being intermediate (~500-700 MPa)
nodes.solves: The stress to induce martensite is lowest near [001] and higher at [112]: the [001] pillar transforms from ~430 MPa while the [112] pillar reaches ~595 MPa with no transformation plateau
nodes.note: read from the 0-1200 MPa colour bar over the discretised triangle; cell values are not printed
nodes.detail: o21: MD transformation stress is lowest at the [001] corner (~150-250 MPa) and rises toward [-111] (~1000-1200 MPa), the [112] region being intermediate (~500-700 MPa)

nodes.title: evidence, F8
nodes.head: In the herringbone CRSS map the [001] corner cell is still several times lower (~40-60 MPa) than the rest of the triangle (~150-300 MPa), so that CRSS is not orientation independent either
nodes.solves: The operative transformation is the herringbone B2-B19' MT that produces (001)B19' compound twins, not the conventional B2-B19' MT with [011]B19' type II twins
nodes.note: the linked text claims only 'significantly less variation' and does not mention the surviving [001] outlier
